2609.19441.title: Predict Before You Deploy: Offline Prediction of Quantization-Induced Task Degradation for World Action Models
2609.19441.paper_summary: World action models (WAMs) rely on video-generation backbones, requiring substantial memory and compute for deployment. Post-training quantization reduces memory and can accelerate inference, but bit width, grouping, and quantizer choice define a large configuration space. Identifying configurations that preserve task performance through exhaustive closed-loop evaluation is costly. We propose PreDE (Predict Before You Deploy), a policy-calibrated framework for predicting quantization-induced task degradation from offline action deviations. Using closed-loop outcomes from a small development set, PreDE calibrates two thresholds and accepts, rejects, or defers new configurations using a fixed observation log. Under a within-setting label-ordering hypothesis, the rule issues decisions where all thresholds consistent with the development labels agree. Across five WAMs and four benchmark settings, quantization produces configuration-dependent task losses that cannot be explained by bit width alone or a shared deviation threshold. Across 28 held-out configurations from two policies, PreDE issued 21 decisions before observing closed-loop outcomes (75% coverage), all matching the observed acceptable or degraded labels. Deferred candidates included both acceptable outcomes and a 33-percentage-point loss. In 450 Franka Research 3 trials across two independently fine-tuned policies, all configurations assigned to high-deviation groups before testing showed significant degradation, while low-deviation comparisons showed no statistically significant degradation. On the real robot, W4A4 achieved a 1.37x action-query speedup and approximately 44% lower peak memory. These results support policy-specific behavioral calibration for quantization configuration selection while identifying candidates that require closed-loop evaluation. The code is available at https://github.com/jiuyixu25/PreDE.
2609.19441.paper_summary_zh: 世界行動模型（WAMs）依賴於視頻生成骨幹，這需要大量的內存和計算資源來進行部署。訓練後量化可以減少內存並加速推理，但位寬、分組和量化器的選擇定義了一個龐大的配置空間。通過徹底的閉環評估來識別保留任務性能的配置是成本高昂的。我們提出了PreDE（預測後再部署），這是一個政策校準框架，用於從離線行動偏差中預測量化引起的任務退化。利用來自小型開發集的閉環結果，PreDE校準了兩個閾值，並使用固定的觀察日誌接受、拒絕或延遲新的配置。在一個內部設定的標籤排序假設下，該規則在所有與開發標籤一致的閾值同意的情況下發出決策。在五個WAMs和四個基準設定中，量化產生的任務損失依賴於配置，這不能僅通過位寬或共享偏差閾值來解釋。在來自兩個政策的28個保留配置中，PreDE在觀察到閉環結果之前發出了21個決策（75% 覆蓋率），所有決策均與觀察到的可接受或退化標籤相匹配。延遲的候選者包括可接受的結果和33個百分點的損失。在450次Franka Research 3的試驗中，所有在測試前被分配到高偏差組的配置顯示出顯著的退化，而低偏差的比較則未顯示出統計上顯著的退化。在真實機器人上，W4A4實現了1.37倍的行動查詢加速和約44%的峰值內存降低。這些結果支持針對量化配置選擇的政策特定行為校準，同時識別需要閉環評估的候選者。代碼可在 https://github.com/jiuyixu25/PreDE 獲得。
